title: Workbench refinement sweep: workflow, evidence and reader experience
summary: The user accepted all R01-R11 refinements after a four-choice decision interview. Workflow gates, source inspection, navigation and research summaries are repaired and covered by clean-checkout regressions; original scores and separately owned BR-042 work are preserved.

links.label: Original proposal and decision history: Git recovery

decision_provenance: The user requested a full sweep, then a decision interview followed by fixes. After the four-choice interview, the user explicitly replied “all your rec”, accepting conservative control reuse, notice-complete preview retention, parking the three calibration ideas, the scoped BR-042 issue, and implementation of the full refinement pass. This authorizes maintenance and editorial fixes, not model trials or publication.
reopen_when: A recorded regression recurs, reader feedback reveals a concrete gap, the outstanding preview notice is recovered, or newly maintained methods justify revisiting module boundaries.

decisions: Block reviewed/invalidated control owners until scoped reassessment clears reuse
Retain notice-complete previews with individual restrictions; leave incomplete notices optional
Park the three completed calibration ideas with reopening conditions
Record the scoped BR-042 naming dispute for both affected experiments
Retain all 37 historical execution records; maintain native implementations only where reuse justifies them.
Author compact experiment config and scientific Markdown; generate execution receipts and snapshots.
Allow explicit diagnostic exploration before controls; require verified controls for benchmark claims and promotion.
Flag affected experiments and their summaries/exports, recording affected runs in the issue rather than adding claim-level dependency machinery.
Keep modules, files and normal imports; avoid a generic store, schema migration engine, plugin framework or compatibility shims.

Allow scoped narrower reassessment after partial withdrawal, eligibility of unchanged diagnostic attempts after exact-task controls and reassessment, and explicitly flagged draft exports. None establishes submission readiness.
